title: Sections over the complement of V(I) in Spec A and maps from powers of I
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ a finitely generated ideal and $M$ an $A$-module. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $D=X\setminus V(I)=\{\mathfrak p\in X: I\not\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$, an open subset with $D=\bigcup_{f\in I}D(f)$. Let $\widetilde M$ be the $\mathcal O_X$-module of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], with $\tau_W:M\to\widetilde M(W)$, and for $f\in A$ identify $\widetilde M(D(f))$ with the localization $M_f$ as there ($x/f^k\leftrightarrow f^{-k}\tau_{D(f)}(x)$). Let $I^0=A$ and $I^n$ ($n\ge1$) the $n$-th power of $I$, and $M_n=\{x\in M: ax=0\text{ for all }a\in I^n\}$ (so $M_0=0$); then $I^{n+1}\subseteq I^n$ and $M_n\subseteq M_{n+1}$. (1) For every $n\ge0$ and every $A$-linear $\varphi:I^n\to M$ there is a unique $c_n(\varphi)\in\widetilde M(D)$ with $c_n(\varphi)|_{D(f)}=\varphi(f^n)/f^n\in M_f$ for every $f\in I$; one has $c_{n+1}(\varphi|_{I^{n+1}})=c_n(\varphi)$, and the induced map $\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_A(I^n,M)\to\widetilde M(D)$ (colimit over $n\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with transition maps the restrictions along $I^{n+1}\subseteq I^n$) is injective. (2) For every $n\ge0$ and every $A$-linear $\psi:I^n\to M/M_n$ there is a unique $c'_n(\psi)\in\widetilde M(D)$ with $c'_n(\psi)|_{D(f)}=y/f^n\in M_f$ for every $f\in I$ and every $y\in M$ whose class in $M/M_n$ is $\psi(f^n)$ (the fraction $y/f^n$ does not depend on the choice of $y$, as $f^nM_n=0$); one has $c'_{n+1}(\bar p_n\circ\psi|_{I^{n+1}})=c'_n(\psi)$, where $\bar p_n:M/M_n\to M/M_{n+1}$ is the projection, and the induced map $\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_A(I^n,M/M_n)\to\widetilde M(D)$ (transition maps $\psi\mapsto\bar p_n\circ\psi|_{I^{n+1}}$) is bijective. (3) If for $x\in M$, $Ix=0$ implies $x=0$, then $M_n=0$ for all $n$ and the map of (1) is bijective.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PM (label lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact-open-in-affine, line 3941; tag verified in tags/tags line 2235) and its proof (lines 3962-4089), whose explicit description $\varphi\mapsto(\varphi(f_i^n)/f_i^n)_i$ of the canonical map is used here as its definition; Example 01PN (example-does-not-work-in-general, line 4092) shows the first map need not be surjective

proof.text:
*Step 1 (the cover).* Write $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$ ($t\ge0$). For $\mathfrak p\in X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] one has $I
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p$ iff $f
otin\mathfrak p$ for some $f\in I$ iff $f_i
otin\mathfrak p$ for some $i$ (if all $f_i\in\mathfrak p$ then $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$). Hence $D= igcup_{f\in I}D(f)= igcup_{i=1}^tD(f_i)$, and $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$ since $\mathfrak p$ is prime. (For $t=0$, $I=0$ and $D=\emptyset$.)

source.place: Lemma 01PM, proof, second paragraph: 'Say $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$. Then $\Spec(A)\setminus V(I)=\bigcup D(f_i)$'

proof.text: *Step 2 (sections over $D$ as compatible families; the source's exact sequence $0\to\Gamma(D,\widetilde M)\to\bigoplus_iM_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i,j}M_{f_if_j}$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], $\widetilde M(D(f))=M_f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] via $x/f^k\leftrightarrow f^{-k}\tau_{D(f)}(x)$, and the restriction $\widetilde M(D(f))\to\widetilde M(D(fg))$ is the canonical map $M_f\to M_{fg}$, $x/f^e\mapsto g^ex/(fg)^e$. $\widetilde M$ is a sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; applied to the open covers $D=\bigcup_{f\in S}D(f)$ for $S=I$ or $S=\{f_1,\dots,f_t\}$ (Step 1, with $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$) this gives: (a) a section $s\in\widetilde M(D)$ is determined by its restrictions $s|_{D(f_i)}\in M_{f_i}$, $i=1,\dots,t$; (b) if for every $f\in S$ an element $s_f\in M_f$ is given such that $s_f$ and $s_g$ have the same image in $M_{fg}$ for all $f,g\in S$, there is exactly one $s\in\widetilde M(D)$ with $s|_{D(f)}=s_f$ for all $f\in S$. Equality in $M_f$ is as in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]: $x/f^a=y/f^b$ iff $f^k(f^bx-f^ay)=0$ for some $k$.

source.place: Lemma 01PM, proof, second paragraph: 'Hence $0\to\Gamma(\Spec(A)\setminus V(I),\widetilde M)\to\bigoplus_iM_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i,j}M_{f_if_j}$ is exact'

proof.text: *Step 3 (the maps $c'_n$, $c_n$, their compatibility with the transition maps, and the two canonical maps).* Let $\psi:I^n\to M/M_n$ be $A$-linear. For $f\in I$ choose $y_f\in M$ with class $\psi(f^n)$ (note $f^n\in I^n$). The fraction $y_f/f^n\in M_f$ does not depend on the choice: two choices differ by $z\in M_n$, and $f^nz=0$ as $f^n\in I^n$, so $z/f^n=0$. For $f,g\in I$, the class of $g^ny_f-f^ny_g$ is $g^n\psi(f^n)-f^n\psi(g^n)=\psi(g^nf^n)-\psi(f^ng^n)=0$ ($A$-linearity), so $g^ny_f-f^ny_g\in M_n$ and $(fg)^n\in I^n$ kills it; hence $g^ny_f/(fg)^n=f^ny_g/(fg)^n$, i.e. $y_f/f^n$ and $y_g/g^n$ have the same image in $M_{fg}$ (Step 2). By Step 2(b) with $S=I$ there is exactly one $c'_n(\psi)\in\widetilde M(D)$ with $c'_n(\psi)|_{D(f)}=y_f/f^n$ for all $f\in I$; by this uniqueness $c'_n$ is $A$-linear (for $\psi+\psi'$, $a\psi$ choose $y_f+y'_f$, $ay_f$). For $\varphi:I^n\to M$ put $c_n(\varphi)=c'_n(\pi_n\circ\varphi)$, $\pi_n:M\to M/M_n$; with the choice $y_f=\varphi(f^n)$ this is the unique section with restrictions $\varphi(f^n)/f^n$, as in (1). Transition: for $f\in I$, $(\bar p_n\circ\psi)(f^{n+1})=f\psi(f^n)$ is the class of $fy_f$ in $M/M_{n+1}$, and $fy_f/f^{n+1}=y_f/f^n$ in $M_f$; so by uniqueness $c'_{n+1}(\bar p_n\circ\psi|_{I^{n+1}})=c'_n(\psi)$; likewise $\varphi(f^{n+1})=f\varphi(f^n)$ gives $c_{n+1}(\varphi|_{I^{n+1}})=c_n(\varphi)$. Thus $(c_n)_n$ and $(c'_n)_n$ are cocones on the two systems of $A$-modules (the transition maps are $A$-linear) and induce the two canonical maps out of the colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This writes out the compatibility the source omits ('We omit the verification that this is compatible with the transition maps'); the source's sheaf-theoretic description via $\widetilde{I^n}\to\widetilde M$ is not needed, as the statement takes the algebraic description as definition.

source.place: Lemma 01PM, proof, first and second paragraphs (transition maps; 'Consider the vector of elements $\varphi(f_i^n)/f_i^n\in M_{f_i}$. It is easy to see that this vector maps to zero in the second direct sum')

proof.text: *Step 4 (a power of $I$ inside the ideal of $k$-th powers of the generators).* For $k\ge1$ let $J_k=(f_1^k,\dots,f_t^k)$. Each $f_i\in\sqrt{J_k}$, and $\sqrt{J_k}$ is an ideal, so $I\subseteq\sqrt{J_k}$; $I$ is finitely generated, so by [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power] there is $N\ge1$ with $I^N\subseteq J_k$, and then $I^{N'}\subseteq J_k$ for all $N'\ge N$; so we may take $N\ge k$. (The source takes $N=t(k-1)+1$: $I^N$ is generated by the monomials $f_1^{e_1}\cdots f_t^{e_t}$, $\sum e_i=N$, and in each some $e_i\ge k$; only the existence of $N$ is used below.) In particular every $a\in I^N$ is $\sum_ib_if_i^k$ with $b_i\in A$.

source.place: Lemma 01PM, proof, third paragraph: 'It is easy to see that this means that $\varphi|_{I^{t(n+m-1)+1}}=0$', and fourth-to-last paragraph (the monomials of degree $t(n-1)+1$)

proof.text: *Step 5 (injectivity in (1)).* By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise](1) every element of $\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_A(I^n,M)$ is the image $\iota_n(\varphi)$ of some $\varphi:I^n\to M$. Suppose $c_n(\varphi)=0$. Then $\varphi(f_i^n)/f_i^n=0$ in $M_{f_i}$ for every $i$ (Step 3, $f_i\in I$), so $f_i^{m}\varphi(f_i^n)=0$ for some $m$, which we take $\ge1$ and common to all $i$ (Step 2). Hence $\varphi(f_i^{n+m})=f_i^m\varphi(f_i^n)=0$. Take $N\ge n+m$ with $I^N\subseteq J_{n+m}$ (Step 4). Every $a\in I^N$ is $\sum_ib_if_i^{n+m}$ with $f_i^{n+m}\in I^n$, so $\varphi(a)=\sum_ib_i\varphi(f_i^{n+m})=0$: the image of $\varphi$ in $\operatorname{Hom}_A(I^N,M)$ under the composite transition map (restriction to $I^N$) is $0$, hence $\iota_n(\varphi)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise](2). So the map of (1) is injective.

source.place: Lemma 01PM, proof, third paragraph ('Let us show that the first arrow is injective using this description')

proof.text: *Step 6 (injectivity in (2); the source omits it).* As in Step 5 an element of $\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_A(I^n,M/M_n)$ is $\iota_n(\psi)$ for some $\psi:I^n\to M/M_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise](1). Suppose $c'_n(\psi)=0$; choose $y_i\in M$ with class $\psi(f_i^n)$. Then $y_i/f_i^n=0$ in $M_{f_i}$, so $f_i^my_i=0$ for a common $m\ge1$, and $\psi(f_i^{n+m})=f_i^m\psi(f_i^n)$ is the class of $f_i^my_i=0$. With $N\ge n+m$, $I^N\subseteq J_{n+m}$ (Step 4) we get $\psi|_{I^N}=0$ as in Step 5. The composite transition map from stage $n$ to stage $N$ sends $\psi$ to $\bar p\circ\psi|_{I^N}$, $\bar p:M/M_n\to M/M_N$ the projection, which is therefore $0$; so $\iota_n(\psi)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise](2).

source.place: Lemma 01PM, proof, last paragraph: 'We omit the proof of injectivity' (written out here along the lines of the third paragraph)

proof.text: *Step 7 (surjectivity in (2)).* Let $s\in\widetilde M(D)$. For each $i$, $s|_{D(f_i)}=x_i/f_i^{n_i}\in M_{f_i}$ (Step 2); since $x/f^a=f^bx/f^{a+b}$ we may use one exponent $n\ge1$ for all $i$. The restrictions of $s|_{D(f_i)}$ and $s|_{D(f_j)}$ to $D(f_if_j)$ agree, i.e. $f_j^nx_i/(f_if_j)^n=f_i^nx_j/(f_if_j)^n$, so $(f_if_j)^m(f_j^nx_i-f_i^nx_j)=0$ for some $m$, common to all pairs (Step 2). Replacing $x_i$ by $f_i^mx_i$ and $n$ by $n+m$ (which does not change $x_i/f_i^n$) we get $f_j^nx_i=f_i^nx_j$ in $M$ for all $i,j$. Put $K_n=\{x\in M: f_1^nx=\dots=f_t^nx=0\}$ and take $N\ge n$ with $I^N\subseteq J_n$ (Step 4). Define $\varphi:I^N\to M/K_n$ by $\varphi(\sum_ib_if_i^n)=$ class of $\sum_ib_ix_i$ ($b_i\in A$). It is well defined: if $\sum_ib_if_i^n=0$ and $z=\sum_ib_ix_i$, then for every $j$, $f_j^nz=\sum_ib_if_i^nx_j=0$ by the relations, so $z\in K_n$; and it is $A$-linear. (The source defines $\varphi$ on the monomial generators of $I^{t(n-1)+1}$, writing each monomial as $f^{E-ne_{i(E)}}\cdot f_{i(E)}^n$, and checks relations by the same computation.) Since $J_n$ kills $K_n$ and $I^N\subseteq J_n$, $K_n\subseteq M_N$; let $\psi:I^N\to M/M_N$ be $\varphi$ followed by the projection $M/K_n\to M/M_N$. For each $i$, $f_i^N=f_i^{N-n}f_i^n$, so $\psi(f_i^N)$ is the class of $f_i^{N-n}x_i$, and by Step 3 $c'_N(\psi)|_{D(f_i)}=f_i^{N-n}x_i/f_i^N=x_i/f_i^n=s|_{D(f_i)}$. By Step 2(a), $c'_N(\psi)=s$, so $s$ is the image of $\iota_N(\psi)$. With Step 6 the map of (2) is bijective.

source.place: Lemma 01PM, proof, fifth and sixth paragraphs ('Let us attempt to construct an inverse of the second map' through 'This proves the second arrow of the lemma is surjective')

proof.text: *Step 8 (the torsion-free case (3)).* Assume $Ix=0\Rightarrow x=0$. Then $M_n=0$ by induction: $M_0=0$; if $I^{n+1}x=0$, then for every $a\in I^n$, $I(ax)\subseteq I^{n+1}x=0$, so $ax=0$; thus $x\in M_n=0$. Hence $M/M_n=M$, the transition maps of the system in (2) are those of (1), and $c'_n(\psi)=c_n(\psi)$ (choose $y_f=\psi(f^n)$ in Step 3); so the map of (1) is the map of (2) [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], bijective by Steps 6 and 7.

source.place: Lemma 01PM, proof, fourth paragraph: 'Note that each $M_n=0$ in case we have $Ix=0\Rightarrow x=0$'

theorem sections_over_quasiCompactOpen_of_affine
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (I : Ideal A) (hIfg : I.FG)
    (D : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens)
    (hD : ∀ (p : PrimeSpectrum A), p ∈ D ↔ ¬ ∀ a : A, a ∈ I → a ∈ p.asIdeal)
    (N : ℕ → Submodule A M)
    (hN : ∀ n x, x ∈ N n ↔ ∀ a : A, a ∈ I ^ n → a • x = 0) :
    ∃ (r : ∀ (n m : ℕ), n ≤ m →
        (ModuleCat.of A (I ^ m : Ideal A) ⟶ ModuleCat.of A (I ^ n : Ideal A)))
      (q : ∀ (n m : ℕ), n ≤ m →
        (ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ N n) ⟶ ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ N m)))
      (F G : ℕ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u})
      (e : ∀ n, F.obj n ≅ AddCommGrpCat.of
        (ModuleCat.of A (I ^ n : Ideal A) ⟶ ModuleCat.of A M))
      (e' : ∀ n, G.obj n ≅ AddCommGrpCat.of
        (ModuleCat.of A (I ^ n : Ideal A) ⟶ ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ N n)))
      (c : F ⟶ (Functor.const ℕ).obj
        (AddCommGrpCat.of Γ(tilde (R := CommRingCat.of A) (ModuleCat.of A M), D)))
      (c' : G ⟶ (Functor.const ℕ).obj
        (AddCommGrpCat.of Γ(tilde (R := CommRingCat.of A) (ModuleCat.of A M), D))),
      (∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m) (x : (I ^ m : Ideal A)),
        (r n m h x : A) = (x : A)) ∧
      (∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m) (x : M),
        q n m h ((N n).mkQ x) = (N m).mkQ x) ∧
      (∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m)
        (φ : ModuleCat.of A (I ^ n : Ideal A) ⟶ ModuleCat.of A M),
        (e m).hom (F.map (homOfLE h) ((e n).inv φ)) = r n m h ≫ φ) ∧
      (∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m)
        (ψ : ModuleCat.of A (I ^ n : Ideal A) ⟶ ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ N n)),
        (e' m).hom (G.map (homOfLE h) ((e' n).inv ψ)) = r n m h ≫ ψ ≫ q n m h) ∧
      (∀ (f : A) (hf : f ∈ I), ∃ hle : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f ≤ D,
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (φ : ModuleCat.of A (I ^ n : Ideal A) ⟶ ModuleCat.of A M),
          (tilde (R := CommRingCat.of A) (ModuleCat.of A M)).presheaf.map (homOfLE hle).op
              (c.app n ((e n).inv φ)) =
            StructureSheaf.const (R := A) (φ ⟨f ^ n, Ideal.pow_mem_pow hf n⟩)
              (f ^ n) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)
              (fun p hp ↦ p.asIdeal.primeCompl.pow_mem hp n)) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ)
          (ψ : ModuleCat.of A (I ^ n : Ideal A) ⟶ ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ N n))
          (y : M), (N n).mkQ y = ψ ⟨f ^ n, Ideal.pow_mem_pow hf n⟩ →
          (tilde (R := CommRingCat.of A) (ModuleCat.of A M)).presheaf.map (homOfLE hle).op
              (c'.app n ((e' n).inv ψ)) =
            StructureSheaf.const (R := A) y (f ^ n) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)
              (fun p hp ↦ p.asIdeal.primeCompl.pow_mem hp n))) ∧
      Function.Injective (colimit.desc F
        ⟨AddCommGrpCat.of Γ(tilde (R := CommRingCat.of A) (ModuleCat.of A M), D), c⟩) ∧
      Function.Bijective (colimit.desc G
        ⟨AddCommGrpCat.of Γ(tilde (R := CommRingCat.of A) (ModuleCat.of A M), D), c'⟩) ∧
      ((∀ x : M, (∀ a : A, a ∈ I → a • x = 0) → x = 0) →
        Function.Bijective (colimit.desc F
          ⟨AddCommGrpCat.of Γ(tilde (R := CommRingCat.of A) (ModuleCat.of A M), D), c⟩))
